items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1979-03-26
items.q: And, uh, in the next group that was together for two and a half years without, almost without a break, we had, uh, Rhodes Cook on piano. We had, uh, Bobby Turley, who was well known on drums. He played with a lot of big, clean bands. And, uh, Red Roundtree, who was later to be a staff guitarist with

ctx.x: This is good stuff. Yeah. I'm just trying to follow up. That's what I keep a list of questions here for. Yeah.

Dick Coleman was, uh, a banjo player. Wow. And a vocalist, and he was very good. He was, uh, he went to the University of Alabama. He was a Kappa Alpha. And extremely popular with the ladies. Uh-huh. And, uh, so he was, uh, one of the original members of the Brothers Brumelty Boys, also. See, this thing went through so many changes. I, uh, the original Brothers Brumelty Boys, uh, Pruitt and Dick Coleman were both in that band. Uh-huh. And, uh, Dick, uh, he was with a lot of different bands. And, uh, he and Pruitt…
Well, uh, we won't, maybe we can do another reel, huh? Uh-huh. And talk, talk about Mississippi musicians. Of course, I want to talk about a lot of people. I don't know where Bert Sigerson is now.

items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1978-12-03
items.q: who included Red Roundtree and Buddy Seaton on drums... And Red Roundtree was a very famous banjo player who played with Lute Speed... I had recently been out to see him and jammed with me at all.

ctx.x: I didn't get what he played. Well, actually, this was just a little trio.

And, it was Jack and Terry Sheehan up in, uh, Thomas John, and William Gramsson, and all that stuff. And, they played all the society dances, and they played the Fiori roof garden. And, this particular man, this guy, who I was talking about, uh, was, uh, Asian. He hired them. And, uh, so I guess the buddies then, uh, who, uh, who, uh, were, uh, uh, who, uh, were included the Red Round Tree and Buddy Seeky and drums and, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um,…
No, that's right. You didn't tell me much about New Orleans, you tripped down.
